subject: Sprint slot allocation scenario analysis for upcoming pilot
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: PilotOps <pilot-ops@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint slot allocation scenario analysis for upcoming pilot

Team —

Quick context: NimbleHealth confirmed a two-week pilot that will start in early July. They want a predictable burst lane for inference during peak hours and have asked about guaranteed GPU slots for their first sprints. Product wants to avoid a long-term carveout until we have usage signals, but Sales/CS need a clear answer for contractual language.

Current baseline (approx):
- Dedicated pool total: 120 GPU slots (A100-equivalent)
- Average committed reserved: 72 slots across all enterprise pilots
- Typical headroom for short bursts: ~18 slots

Ask: I need a short scenario analysis to bring to leadership and to include in the MLP (mutual launch plan). Please respond with the items below by EOD Friday (May 14):
1) Infra/Runtime (Marcus + Dev): for a 72-hour pilot peak window, what are three feasible allocation approaches (static carveout, timeboxed reservation, dynamic priority band) and the expected tail latency impact at 95th pct? Include fallback behavior if autoscaler evicts.
2) Product (Laura): recommended policy for granting temporary exemptions to autoscaling for pilots — what approval path do we require and what SLAs should we promise?
3) GTM/CS (Neha): minimum contractual language / mutual action items we should commit to NimbleHealth for a timeboxed reservation.

I attached a simple workbook with three demand scenarios and the current pool utilization export. Also included a draft of our autoscale exception checklist.

This is cross-functional and I expect short bullets. I will synthesize into a one-page scenario matrix for leadership. Thanks —

Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slot-scenarios.xlsx, current-pool-usage.csv, autoscale-exceptions.md

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, PilotOps <pilot-ops@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint slot allocation scenario analysis for upcoming pilot

Thanks Sean —

Quick clarifying Q before the analysis: is NimbleHealth expecting sustained 60+ slots during peak, or are they targeting short sub-hour spikes? The scenarios will differ significantly.

My initial thinking (high level):
- Timeboxed reservation (48–72h) with explicit start/end times is least risky for other pilots and easiest to bill.
- Dynamic priority band works if we can quantify the expected token throughput; needs an SLA on cold-start latency.

I'll draft policy bullets for approvals (owner: Product Ops) and include recommended SLA ranges. Sending update tomorrow.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Console

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, PilotOps <pilot-ops@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint slot allocation scenario analysis for upcoming pilot

Sean / team —

See quick tech sketch below (bullets to keep concise):

1) Static carveout (e.g., reserve 24 slots for entire sprint):
   - Pros: deterministic latency, easy to reason about in contract
   - Cons: reduces available capacity for others; poor utilization if pilot doesn't use it
   - 95th pct latency impact: +5–10ms vs baseline for colocated workloads (negligible)
   - Fallback: if pool pressure > 95th pct, we can route new requests to a lower-cost model variant; graceful degrade path defined in runbook INF-2304

2) Timeboxed reservation (48–72h window):
   - Pros: balances utilization and guarantee; ops can reclaim after window
   - Cons: scheduling friction around start times; requires runbook ops handoff
   - 95th pct latency impact: +8–15ms during heavy simultaneous cold-starts
   - Fallback: autoscaler allowed to evict only if critical infra events; eviction triggers an automated alert and contract penalty logic (CS to coordinate)

3) Dynamic priority band (runtime assigns higher priority tokens during peak):
   - Pros: highest overall utilization; minimal wasted slots
   - Cons: may cause tail latency variability for other tenants; requires tighter KPI monitoring
   - 95th pct latency impact: +15–30ms under heavy contention (depends on sequence lengths)
   - Fallback: degrade to timeboxed reservation for the remainder of pilot window if variability exceeds threshold

Operational asks for Infra:
- We need a one-click temporary reservation flow in Console so CS can book a timeboxed window without manual ops intervention.
- Add automated rollback hook in autoscaler (INF-2304).

I can take the workbook and run a quick sim for the three demand scenarios — will return numbers by EOD Thursday.

— Marcus
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sprint slot allocation scenario analysis for upcoming pilot

Folks —

After reviewing the high level options, Product Ops will approve a timeboxed reservation for NimbleHealth (48h window with an optional 24h extension) under these conditions:
- CS signs the timeboxed SLA language (will provide a one-paragraph commitment).
- Ops retains right to evict for critical infra incidents; eviction triggers a credit calculation.
- Any autoscale exception must be logged in the exceptions tracker and pre-approved by Ops lead.

Neha — please draft the one-paragraph contractual language and confirm whether NimbleHealth expects sustained slot consumption or short spikes (Laura's Q). Marcus / Dev — please finalize the simulation numbers and runbook hooks (INF-2304) by EOD Thursday so I can include them in the approval note.

I'll coordinate the approval signature (Product Ops -> Infra Lead -> Finance for billing note). Ops will schedule oncall coverage during the window.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
